name: agent-usage
description: Roughly how much memory and CPU each agent's processes use, and its tokens per model: a footer column, warnings over thresholds, /agent-usage, the agent_usage tool (compact JSON, detail on request), agent_reap (kills a stopped agent's leftovers through Bash), an optional snapshot file and a low-memory notice

memoryThresholdGB.title: Memory threshold (GB)
memoryThresholdGB.description: Warn when one agent's processes together use more than this much memory (PSS).

cpuThresholdPercent.title: CPU threshold (% of one core)
cpuThresholdPercent.description: Warn when one agent's processes together use more than this much CPU; 100 is one core.

footer.title: Footer
footer.description: always: a column in the footer, right of live-tests, of the rows over the footer floors, ⚠ on rows over a threshold; alerts: only a status line while one is over; off: neither.

footerMinMemoryMB.title: Footer floor: memory (MB)
footerMinMemoryMB.description: The footer column shows a row (an agent, claude, untracked) only over this much memory or over the CPU floor.

footerMinCpuPercent.title: Footer floor: CPU (% of one core)
footerMinCpuPercent.description: The footer column shows a row only over this much CPU or over the memory floor.

intervalSeconds.title: Sample interval (seconds)
intervalSeconds.description: How often the processes are measured.

memoryFloorMB.title: Memory floor (MB)
memoryFloorMB.description: When MemAvailable drops under this plus the margin, the main conversation gets one notice naming the biggest agents; it re-arms once memory is back. 0 is off.

pressureMarginMB.title: Pressure margin (MB)
pressureMarginMB.description: How far above the floor the notice fires.

snapshotPath.title: Snapshot file
snapshotPath.description: Absolute path rewritten with the agent_usage JSON every sample, for scripts to read. Empty is off.

reapOnStop.title: Reap on stop
reapOnStop.description: Off by default. When on, 30 s after an agent goes from live to stopped or gone, its leftover processes (what agent_usage lists as unattributed for it) are killed through the Bash tool, as agent_reap does, so the permission check and sandbox still apply, and the main conversation gets one notice listing what was killed.
